CONSTRAINTS: You arrive at Richmond District at 9:00AM. Matthew will be at The Castro from 4:30PM to 8:00PM. You'd like to meet Matthew for a minimum of 45 minutes. Rebecca will be at Nob Hill from 3:15PM to 7:15PM. You'd like to meet Rebecca for a minimum of 105 minutes. Brian will be at Marina District from 2:15PM to 10:00PM. You'd like to meet Brian for a minimum of 30 minutes. Emily will be at Pacific Heights from 11:15AM to 7:45PM. You'd like to meet Emily for a minimum of 15 minutes. Karen will be at Haight-Ashbury from 11:45AM to 5:30PM. You'd like to meet Karen for a minimum of 30 minutes. Stephanie will be at Mission District from 1:00PM to 3:45PM. You'd like to meet Stephanie for a minimum of 75 minutes. James will be at Chinatown from 2:30PM to 7:00PM. You'd like to meet James for a minimum of 120 minutes. Steven will be at Russian Hill from 2:00PM to 8:00PM. You'd like to meet Steven for a minimum of 30 minutes. Elizabeth will be at Alamo Square from 1:00PM to 5:15PM. You'd like to meet Elizabeth for a minimum of 120 minutes. William will be at Bayview from 6:15PM to 8:15PM. You'd like to meet William for a minimum of 90 minutes.

Your response should start with 'SOLUTION:'.

Please output the meeting schedule in the following JSON format:
{"itinerary": [{"action": "meet", "person": "<PERSON_NAME>", "start_time": "<HH:MM>", "end_time": "<HH:MM>"}]}. Make sure to include the person's name for each meeting.

SOLUTION:
One effective “optimal‐by count” schedule we arrived at is to use the early day (after your 9:00 Richmond District arrival) to meet the two friends with short “morning‐window” visits and then—in the afternoon—choose the five meetings that require relatively little time. In our working example you meet Emily and Karen in the late–morning, then in the afternoon you visit Stephanie (whose 75‑minute meeting is forced into her 13:00–15:45 Mission District window), then use two very short meetings (30 minutes each) with Steven (at Russian Hill) and Brian (at Marina District), then meet Matthew at The Castro for 45 minutes and finally meet William at Bayview for 90 minutes. (The longer‐duration options at Nob Hill, Chinatown or Alamo Square could not all be “stacked” without overrunning one or more friend’s window.) 

A sample timeline is as follows (note that travel and waiting times have been “built‐in” so that every meeting falls entirely within the friend’s available window):

• Start at Richmond District at 9:00AM.
• Depart early so that you get to Pacific Heights in time to meet Emily as soon as her window opens.
  – Meet Emily at Pacific Heights from 11:15AM to 11:30AM.
• Then travel to Haight-Ashbury (about 11 minutes from Pacific Heights) and meet Karen from 11:45AM to 12:15PM.
• Next, head to Mission District (≈11 minutes from Haight-Ashbury) so that by waiting a few minutes you can begin your meeting with Stephanie at 1:00PM. Meet her for 75 minutes (until 2:15PM) – note that her window is 1:00PM–3:45PM.
  In our sample we set Stephanie’s meeting 1:00–2:15PM (75 minutes).
• After Stephanie you travel from Mission District to Russian Hill (≈15 minutes) arriving about 2:30PM and meet Steven for 30 minutes (2:30–3:00PM; his window is 2:00PM–8:00PM).
• Immediately from Russian Hill (only a 7‑minute trip) go to Marina District arriving around 3:07PM and meet Brian from about 3:07PM until 3:37PM (he’s available 2:15PM–10:00PM).
• Then you head from Marina District to The Castro (≈22 minutes) so that by waiting a bit you can begin your meeting with Matthew at 4:30PM. Meet Matthew for 45 minutes from 4:30PM to 5:15PM (he is at The Castro 4:30PM–8:00PM).
• Finally, travel from The Castro to Bayview (≈19 minutes) so you can be at Bayview in time for William’s available window. His meeting (90 minutes) is scheduled from 6:15PM to 7:45PM (William is at Bayview 6:15PM–8:15PM).

In the above sample the waiting intervals (for example, arriving early at The Castro then waiting for Matthew’s window, or arriving early at Bayview and waiting for 6:15PM) are “free‐time” that result from the neighborhood travel times and friend availability. This plan meets a total of 7 friends—the two available in the morning plus the five afternoon visits—while ensuring each meeting meets the minimum contact duration required.
